profile.headline: Software Engineer @ General Motors
profile.summary:
Driven and self-starting electrical engineering grad working in the automotive industry. 

Following my graduation from Michigan State University's Honors College I began my professional career at General Motor's within the TRACK rotational program. After completing my 3 rotations, I have since worked as an embedded software engineer within the Vehicle Mechatronics Embedded Controls organization, specifically working on software related to Battery Energy Transfer.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Acted as interim scrum lead for a 10-week PI overseeing PI planning facilitation, risk management, and daily stand-up tracking. Successfully delivered 34 of 36 art features planned for completion.
• Developed MISRA and GM-standards compliant production embedded C software across electrification display specific algorithms - Vehicle Range, Customer-Usable State of Charge, Battery Energy Usage Tracking, Battery State of Health - in support of improving the vehicle experience for GM EVs.
• Championed code quality and engineering standardization across the scrum’s software stack. Built and socialized an agentic PR review tool to enforce GM specific and industry best practices. Introduced a dashboard to track various GM coding standards across 24 scrum-owned software components. Converted four software components to follow CppUTest formatting, increasing code coverage from 90% to 100%.
• Developed embedded C software to meet UN GTR 22 regulatory requirements impacting all light duty BEVs and PHEVs through the creation of several new DIDs. Facilitated requirements development, software implementation, and validation of the solution through unit and integration testing.
• Led vehicle-level validation of 15+ software patches using INCA and Vehicle Spy. Identified and root caused four separate existing logic issues to prevent future software patches.
• Designed 50+ Gherkin-based behavioral integration-level tests for CI/CD validation. Led discussions with systems engineers to develop robust requirements for electrification driver display software functionalities.
• Generated a MATLAB script to automate the generation of an interface matrix for use in software component FMEAs. Reduce processing time for developers by 1-2 hours.

positions.title: Dev QA (TRACK)
positions.description:
• Automated 36 functional integration test cases for vehicle applications using Gherkin syntax and Appium framework.
• Conducted manual bench and emulator based quality assurance testing of 7 different Ultifi and DFF vehicle applications.
• Led sync-up meetings with the integration team to compile and coordinate the testing of s 70-case test suite for a high-priority Ultifi application.
• Assisted senior engineers with triaging issues in the initiation of a CI/CD pipeline for Ultifi application software.

positions.title: Project Engineer for Active Safety Products (TRACK)
positions.description:
• Created additional functionality and efficiency for team Macro tools through VBA coding.
• Triaged and communicated issues relating to the Video Processing Module for light and heavy duty trucks.

positions.title: Feature Integration Engineer (TRACK)
positions.description:
• Collaborated with spec owners & developers to test NIDS feature utilizing Vehicle Spy and simulated back-office commands.
• Refined and created new onboarding documentation for future FIEs.

positions.title: Varsity Receiver/Defensive Back Coach
positions.description:
RESPONSIBILITIES (3):
-Employ verbal communication skills as well as visual instructions to teach both receivers and defensive backs proper fundamentals
-Interface with coaching staff to organize and plan practices, game strategy, and roster changes throughout an 11 week season
-Analyze the opposing team’s tendencies from the press box to assist the coordinators in strategic play calling and game management

PROUDEST ACHIEVEMENTS (1):
-Being able to coach the 2020-2021 Varsity team who was able to win the first ever football state championship for DeWitt

positions.title: Electrical Engineering Intern
positions.description:
RESPONSIBILITIES (5):
-Designed a printed circuit board (PCB) capable of being used for temperature rise testing on compliant eye pin populations. The board was designed using the Mentor Xpedition development software and allowed the team to conduct two stages of testing during my internship
-Interfaced with internal stakeholders such as the compliant pin team and test manager to refine the design of the test board. Created multiple revisions using NX modeling software and settled on an array design which would allow for testing simplicity and flexibility
-Created board designs to support three other compliant pin sizes after test verification of the original board design. These boards will allow the team to obtain similar on-board temperature rise data in the future
-Communicated with suppliers, customers, and internal stakeholders to support customer standards and requests
-Produced PCB models and technical drawings in NX to view the connection of a board with a new header product

PROUDEST ACHIEVEMENTS (1):
-Being able to take a self lead PCB design project from the initial conceptual stages all the way through the intended use testing stages within my internship time frame

positions.title: AutoDrive Challenge - Hardware Team
positions.description:
Participated in the SAE sponsored AutoDrive Challenge which is a 4 year competition aimed at enabling level 4 autonomous driving in a simulated urban environment by the end of the competition. Within the team I served as a member on the Electrical Hardware team with my fellow student, Alex Walton, wherein we worked to design and build two power monitoring devices to enhance safety and redundancy of the vehicle.

RESPONSIBILITIES (3):
-Analyze component data sheets to evaluate and select compatible parts to be utilized in our power management system designs
-Composed a C program utilized by a Teensy 4.0 to constantly check the V-I characteristics of our main car power bus and output results to a connected usb
-Utilized KiCad EDA software to create a schematic and layout for a distributed power management and monitoring system that could be placed in the vehicle to monitor power going to various peripherals

PROUDEST ACHIEVEMENTS (1):
-Designed and assembled a functioning general power monitoring board that could accurately measure the voltage, current, and power of the 13.8 V in-vehicle power bus.

positions.title: Technical Intern
positions.description:
I had the opportunity to participate in the GE Intern Academy, a program devised in light of the Covid pandemic of 2020. The month long internship focused on learning the technology of the aviation business as well as the industry as a whole. In addition, a great amount of time was placed into developing my leadership and professional skills. In culmination of the internship, I was able to participate in an industry relevant business simulation with a group of my fellow interns and pitch our ideas and plan to a panel of reviewers.

RESPONSIBILITIES (3):
-Acquired knowledge on the principles of jet engines, flight and power systems, and LEAN manufacturing through assignments, small group sessions, and educational lectures
-Improved leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills through small group discussions, judged presentations, and informational interviewing opportunities
-Translated teachings into action in an industry relevant business simulation that required teamwork and working fast under pressure which was then presented to a panel of reviewers for judging

PROUDEST ACHIEVEMENTS (2):
-Designed and pitched a "social impact hackathon" aimed at developing 3D printed water filters to provide to areas in need through collaborating with a group outside of work hours 
-Prepared and presented three tollgate reviews for a New Product Introduction that my group developed through analyzing business capabilities and market data which received very positive feedback from our reviewers.

positions.title: Summer Engineering Entrepreneurship Experience
positions.description:
With my Summer 2020 internship shortened due to the Covid-19 pandemic, I decided to participate in the inaugural Summer Engineering Entrepreneurship Experience. The program was a combination of entrepreneurial education and small group meetings aimed at identifying a problem followed by developing a creative solution and product design.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES (4):
-Collaborated with a group of peers to learn about the process of starting a business and the early challenges associated with it
-Learned more about the app design and implementation steps by using LinkedIn ProFinder to recieve quotes and ideas for an app build
-Generated market and consumer demand insights through surveying and researching similar products, which led to the selection of a bus tracker and schedule builder integration app for our small group focus
-Created a wireframe for the app using Adobe XD which was then used to discuss the idea with outside developers

FUN FACT (1):
-Connected with two MSU alums who shared their experiences in the app development world post-college and provided feedback on my groups idea

positions.title: Professorial Assistant
positions.description:
Research assistant in the advertising field. Currently involved with conducting research analyzing psychophysiological effects of various advertising techniques and trends.

-Collaborate with a team of 10 individuals to discuss best research practices and implementation techniques
-Collected psychophysiological data for over 30 participants within two published lab studies
-Delivered lab backed evidence to the Detroit Zoo to validate their marketing campaign calling on the relaxing effects of animals
-Presented research describing the effect of candidate orientation and placement on ad evaluation and planned interaction at the University Undergraduate Research and Arts Forum

positions.title: Strategic Support Associate
positions.description:
-Receive real time transactional documents and enter relevant data into Jackson database to enable functionality of other business units
-Verify NAIC certification of producers
-Process client/broker dealer requested changes of producers on retirement policies
-Asked to quality check producer of record changes due to proficiency in processing
-Process indexing changes to ensure up to date accuracy of document information

positions.title: Referee
positions.description: Officiated youth recreational basketball at the 3rd-6th grade level. Helped educate kids on the fundamentals of basketball as well as oversee the proper playing of the game. Created an inclusive and fun environment for young learners of the game.

honors.title: Michigan State Honors College
honors.description: Member of the honors college at Michigan State University.

volunteerExperiences.description: Volunteer "buddy". Assist children with physical/mental ailments in playing the beautiful game of baseball in a fun and structured environment where the parents can sit back and watch.

projects.title: MSU 2019 Spring Design Day Presentation
projects.description: Presented a poster at the Michigan State Design Day event during the 2019 Spring Semester. The poster detailed research done on material strength testing of 3D printed phone cases. Primary data recorded was the tensile and compressional strength and strain of the material. The poster was voted second among EGR 100 participants as selected by various K12 students in attendance.

projects.title: University Undergraduate Research and Arts Forum Presentation
projects.description: Presented a poster detailing the effects on viewer preferences caused by manipulating variables on a political ad. Variables manipulated were the orientation of the candidate, positioning on the poster of the candidate, and the political affiliation of the candidate. research was done in correlation with Dr. Saleem Alhabash, my leading professor for the Professorial Assistantship position I hold at MSU.

publications.title: Effects of candidate lateral location and eye gaze direction in political ads: Evidence from self-report and eye movement patterns
publications.publisher: Political Communication Interest Group of the Association for Education in Journalism and Mass Communication · Jan 1, 2019
